contentSections.heading: The bits that matter are the ramp angle, the tie-down points, and the driver's hands.

paragraphs.text: A wheelchair vehicle is only as good as its worst detail. A ramp that's too steep, a restraint point that doesn't quite line up, a driver who's never actually clipped one in before, any of those turns a five-minute boarding into a stressful one. Ours run a low-angle ramp so you're not fighting gravity to get in, and the securement points are checked before the car leaves the depot, not worked out for the first time at the kerb.

If you use a manual chair, a power chair, or a scooter, tell us which when you book. The vehicle we send, and the way your driver sets it up, changes depending on the answer, and we'd rather ask the question now than guess at the kerb.

contentSections.heading: A 4am flight shouldn't mean a rushed transfer to get there.

contentSections.heading: What Exactly Is a Maxi Taxi and Why Choose One for the Airport?

paragraphs.text: A maxi taxi is a large, people-mover style vehicle, typically a Toyota HiAce or similar, that seats between 7 and 11 passengers comfortably with full luggage. It's the vehicle you book when a standard taxi or rideshare just doesn't cut it.

For Western Sydney Airport runs, a maxi taxi makes more sense than booking multiple cars. Everyone travels together, one driver handles the co-ordination, and you pay a single fixed fare, simpler, cheaper per head, and far less stressful, especially with kids, elderly passengers, or piles of suitcases.

How early should I get to Sydney Airport for a domestic or international flight?

Is there free Wi-Fi at Sydney Airport and how do I connect?

You will be prompted to open a browser window and accept the terms and conditions to get online. This convenient service is perfect for checking emails, contacting family, or getting flight updates before you depart.
What are the luggage storage options at Sydney Airport?

Luggage storage services are conveniently available at the T1 International terminal on the arrivals level. This service, operated by Smarte Carte, provides secure short-term and long-term storage for bags of all sizes, from standard carry-ons to oversized items. It is an excellent solution if you have a long layover or need to store your bags before checking into your hotel. Pricing is based on item size and storage duration.
Can I walk between the domestic and international terminals?

No, walking between the international (T1) and domestic (T2/T3) terminals is not practical as they are located in separate precincts several kilometres apart. For a seamless and reliable transfer, you can use the T-Bus shuttle service or the Airport Link train. The train provides a quick 2-minute journey between the terminals for a fee (around A$6.70 with an Opal card), ensuring you get to your connecting flight on time.
What is the Sydney Airport curfew and how does it affect flights?
The
Sydney Airport

curfew is a government-mandated restriction on aircraft movements between 11 pm and 6 am to reduce noise for local communities. During this time, most passenger flights are not permitted to take off or land. There are some exceptions for emergencies and a limited number of approved flights. This makes booking reliable, on-time transport essential for very early morning departures or late-night arrivals to avoid any travel stress.
What are the accessibility services available for passengers with reduced mobility?
Sydney Airport

is well-equipped to assist passengers with reduced mobility. The terminals feature accessible toilets, ramps, lifts, and designated parking areas. For specific assistance, such as borrowing a wheelchair or receiving help through security and to the boarding gate, it is crucial to pre-book these services directly with your airline at least 48 hours before you travel. This ensures their dedicated staff are prepared to provide a smooth and comfortable experience.
Are there smoking areas at Sydney Airport?

In line with Australian regulations, smoking and vaping are strictly prohibited inside all terminal buildings. However, there are dedicated outdoor smoking areas for passengers and visitors. These designated zones are clearly signposted and located outside the entrances of both the international and domestic terminals. You must use these areas before you pass through security screening, as there are no smoking areas available once you are airside.
